subtitle: A familiar town gains another history

body: Yo-kai Watch 2 is Level-5's Nintendo 3DS role-playing sequel, first released in Japan as two versions later known as Bony Spirits and Fleshy Souls. Nate or Katie must recover a connection with the Yo-kai after losing both the watch and the memories associated with it. The adventure expands the places and creatures surrounding Springdale, with an enlarged roster and another journey behind its everyday troubles. Psychic Specters subsequently extended the same adventure, adding further material to the conflict introduced by the original pair of versions.

Battles retain the six-member medal wheel and three active Yo-kai, allowing the player to rotate companions into the fight. The newer watch introduces G Soultimates, stronger special moves that draw on the soul meters of neighbouring team members. Using one therefore involves the readiness of more than a single creature. Touchscreen interactions continue to support the automatically acting party. The familiar arrangement gains another decision about when to spend a shared resource, especially when a powerful response now could leave nearby companions less prepared for what comes next.

Befriending Yo-kai still involves encountering them and offering suitable food. A new poking interaction allows the player to search for a useful spot on an enemy, producing benefits that can include improved friendship chances or additional rewards. This gives the touchscreen another task during an encounter rather than leaving all attention on the medal wheel. The larger roster makes those individual meetings part of a longer collection. Returning creatures provide continuity, while new forms of interaction give the player more ways to influence how a meeting ends.
